 Judgement

The claimant is the appellant herein seeking enhancement of compensation granted in M.C.O.P.No.313 of 2020 before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Chief Judicial Magistrate Nagendran vs V.Sreedharan on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14819089/
1 Court, Coimbatore.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Chief Judicial Magistrate Nagendran vs V.Sreedharan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per the ranking before the trial Court.

3. The factum of accident, the manner in which the accident had occurred, rash and negligent on the part of driver of the first respondent's vehicle owned by the second respondent insured with the third respondent, are all admitted and hence, the same are hereby confirmed.
The policy is valid as on the date of the accident.
4. On the point of quantum of compensation, both the parties argued.
The claim petitioner has filed the above MCOP claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in the road transport accident that had happened on 01.11.2019.
To substantiate his claim, he has examined himself as PW.1 and also Medical Board records were produced.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P13 were https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis marked and Ex.C1/
medical
disability

report issued by the Medical Board was marked.
5.
On the side of the Insurance Company, RW.1 and RW.2 were examined.
Ex.R1 to Ex.R3 were marked.
Ex . R3
demonstrates that on the date of accident, the policy is in force.
As per Ex.P3 to Ex.P5, the vehicle is duly registered and vehicle is having valid permit and it is as a fitness report also.
As per the medical report/Ex.C1, the petitioner has suffered physical disability of 6%.

6. The nature of the injuries, as reflected in Ex.C1/Medical Board's report is read as follows:-
Diagnosis: closed fracture both bones left leg with left lateral tibial condyle fracture and left clavicle frature at mid 1/3rd.
Procedure done: CRIF with tibial IMIL nail and ORIF with precontoured clavicular plate.
On Examination: Left lowerlimp and shoulder Rom-Full and painful.
On evaluation he is found to have https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis lexomoior disability post traumatic sequelae left upper and lower limbs 06% (Six percentage) of orthopedic disability.
7. The Tribunal accepting the disability, had fixed the same at 6%.

In view of the injuries sustained by the claim petitioner, the Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the injuries resulted in functional disability of the claimant and having satisfied with the facts of the circumstances of the case, has applied the ratio laid down in Manuara Khatun & others -vs- Rajesh Kumar Singh (2017) 4 SCC 796 and applied multiplier method, viz., 9500x12x6%.

entities.text: Manuara Khatun & others -vs- Rajesh Kumar Singh (2017) 4 SCC 796
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since on the date of accident, the injured was 32 years old and multiplier 17 is applied as per the case in Sarla Verma -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation (2009) 6 SCC 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The medical expenses as in medical bills/Ex.P12 amount to Rs.1,29,530/-, has also been awarded.

8. After going through the various heads of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and the quantum of compensation, as awarded by the Tribunal and the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Nagendran vs V.Sreedharan on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14819089/
2 Court of India in Manuara Khatun & others -vs- Rajesh Kumar Singh (supra) and Sarla Verma -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation (supra) was duly adopted by the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Tribunal, this Court finds that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and fair and does not need any interference in this appeal.

entities.text: Supreme Nagendran vs V.Sreedharan on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manuara Khatun & others -vs- Rajesh Kumar Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no infirmity or illegality in the impugned Award passed by the Tribunal.
9. On the point of driver having not possessed valid driving license, the Insurance Company had, on Court summons, examined R.W2 and through him Ex.R2 and R3 were marked.

The trial Court has rightly come to the conclusion that on the date of the accident, though the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license, however, on the date of the accident, the same was expired, as demonstrated by the competent witness to speak about the same, viz., the Assistant from RDO Office, the records from the RDO Office, marked as Exs.R2 and R3, go to show that the driving license of the driver of the offending vehicle was lapsed, and only renew thereafter.
Accordingly, the Tribunal held that the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation, because it amounts to violation of the policy conditions though the policy was in force.
However, following the above judicial pronouncements of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India pay and recovery is rightly ordered by the Tribunal.
The pay and recovery clause awarded by the Tribunal is hereby confirmed.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 10
. Accordingly, this Civil Miscellaneous Petition is dismissed, confirming the Award of the Tribunal.

The 3rd appellant /Insurance Company is directed to deposit the award amount, if not deposited, to the credit of M.C.O.P. No. 313 of 2020 Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal/Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Coimbatore, along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum, from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit, and costs as warded by the Tribunal, less, the amount if any already deposited, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgement.

On such deposit being made, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the award amount,
along with accrued interest and costs as awarded by the Tribunal, less, the amount, if any already withdrawn, by filing necessary application before the Tribunal.
There shall be no order as to costs in this appeal.
